```plato

//==
// # Mesh geometry layers
//
// The whole layered vocabulary of mesh-like geometry: the three generic layers,
// the collection, and the named bindings that pin them to concrete primitives.
// Kept in one file deliberately — the layers and their bindings are one design,
// and splitting them hid the correspondence between a layer and the names that
// instantiate it.
//
// Layer 0 is the vertex data as a view, layer 1 the primitives as a view, and
// layer 2 the indexed storage those primitives are gathered from. Layer 1 is the
// layer most algorithms should target — bounds, area, raycast, transform need to
// see primitives and nothing more, and soups, indexed meshes and tessellated
// procedural surfaces all satisfy it. Layer 2 is the storage layer, needed only
// by welding, adjacency and subdivision-class algorithms that must know which
// primitives share a vertex.
//
// The generic layers are dimension-agnostic, so the plane and space are the same
// tower instantiated twice: a UV domain is the planar instantiation sharing its
// index table with the spatial mesh it parameterizes. The named bindings are
// where dimension arrives, and therefore where the dimensional capabilities
// attach — PointSet, Bounded and Deformable. ITransformable3D is NOT listed
// because IDeformable3D already inherits it (`transforms.concepts.plato`), and
// the Transform bodies for all thirteen representations are derived from Deform
// in `intervals.library.plato`.
//
// Manifoldness, closedness and orientability are deliberately absent: they are
// structural markers in `geometry.concepts.plato`, bolted on per type the way
// `IClosedCurve2D` marks a curve. Element counts and incidence live in
// `topology.concepts.plato`; they are not attached to the layer-2 names because
// a line set has no faces to count.
// Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding, handedness, and normals.

//==
// # The generic layers

// Exposes the points a shape is built from, in a fixed order, generic over the
// embedding. The dimension-agnostic root of the tower.
interface IPointGeometry<TPoint>
    inherits IGeometry
{
    Points(x: Self): Array<TPoint>;
}
```
